text:
anya: Heads up — onboarding magnet-13b (open checkpoint) with int4 quant on dedicated nodes. Basic gen ok but we see divergence / hallucination spike after ~16k tokens in longchain tests. :eyes:

sam: can you paste the minimal repro and the diff vs fp16?

anya: quick repro run (docker job):
```bash
./run_infer --model magnet-13b-int4 --context 65536 --prompt-file long_chain.txt --batch 1 --seed 42 > run.log
```
Logs show stable until ~16000 then token distributions shift and KV readback mismatch appears in dump. Snippet:
```
[00016012] kv_idx_read: 0x7f8a... expected 0x3f2a..., got 0xbf2a...  <-- sign flip?
[00016013] gen_prob: 0.0032 -> 0.49  (sudden)
```

kevin: hmm sign flip sounds like rotary scaling / dtype issue when remapping phase table into int4 kernels. Any repro with fp16 that *doesn't* diverge?

anya: fp16 baseline runs clean through 65k. So it's specific to quant path. I also checked checksum pre/post quant pack — integer packing seems ok.

liz: did you compare rotary position multiplication factors? we had a previous bug where the scale factor used for rot_pos table was computed with float64 and truncated in the int kernel. Try forcing the same float->int rounding path as fp16.

anya: tried forcing identical scale calc in quant kernel (patch below) — small improvement but still drifts after 24k.
```c
// quant_rot_scale.c
float rot_scale = pow(10000.0f, -2.0f * (dim/2) / (float)head_dim);
// patched to match fp16 path (use same denom and clamp)
```

sam: can you dump KV snapshots around the break to compare element-wise between fp16 and int4? maybe a few indices will show systematic phase offset.

anya: already did. diff shows a linear phase offset increasing with timestep index, not random noise. Looks like a per-step accumulation mismatch (drift), not a one-off flip.

ci-bot: automated regression check: magnet-13b-int4 vs magnet-13b-fp16 on longset-50k: quality-bleu: 0.84 -> 0.62 (-26%), avg-perp: 9.1 -> 12.8 (+40%) at 32k+.

tony: could this be an interaction between prefix-caching (we use chunked prefill at 4k) and the quantized kv layout? maybe eviction/merge introduces rebase aligned to 4k boundaries and we lose phase continuity.

kevin: good call. If the kernel uses memcpy with wrong stride rounding when merging shards, phase indices could shift. anya can you run a targeted run with no prefill chunking (single prefill) to see if the drift still grows?

anya: running now (no chunking). preliminary: drift still exists but onset delayed (~28k). So chunking exacerbates it but root cause remains in rotary/packing arithmetic.

liz: next steps I suggest:
- reproduce minimal failing loop with a small synthetic model (reduced dim) to make artifacts obvious
- add unit test comparing rot_matrix(t) produced by fp16 vs quant kernel per-step
- audit memcpy/stride code in kv merge path for int widths

anya: will do. Creating a short synthetic test and opening a small PR with unit test + dump collectors. Assigning to @kevin for kernel audit.

kevin: on it. I will also instrument the pack/unpack to log rounding and clamp events. If we find systematic rounding bias we can fix by adding a compensation table or change quant scale rounding to bankers rounding.

sam: for canary rollout plan — block onboard of magnet-13b-int4 for hosted until we have fix + regression <5% quality drop on longset. Keep dedicated/internal use flagged.

anya: ack. I'll add a smoke test in CI that runs the longctx synthetic for 50k steps to catch this. Patch/PR: https://stash.redwood/infer/PR/5643 :thinking:

kevin: FYI, leaving small note in the kernel README about rotary scale semantics. Might help future bring-ups. :memo:

liz: thanks all. Good debugging thread. Once we have micro repro we can try two mitigation strategies: stricter quant scale alignment or hybrid rot-mult in fp16 for the last 8k tokens. Both have perf tradeoffs.

anya: will update thread with repro assets and test results. If anyone wants early access to the failing logs DM me. :bug:
